## How Many Humanoid Robots Are There in the World?
No one publishes an installed base for humanoid robots.
Axis Intelligence Research built the closest defensible substitute: a cumulative count of units shipped, assembled only from published annual and half-year tracker figures.
**What is the GHSB?** The Global Humanoid Shipped Base (GHSB) is the running total of humanoid robots shipped worldwide since January 1, 2024, read as a floor, central value and upper bound because the three half-year trackers disagree.
It counts units that left a factory, not units still in service.
### GHSB baseline reading, as of June 30, 2026
|Period|Units|Source|
|--|--|--|
|2024 shipments|2,300|Omdia|
|2025 shipments|13,318|Omdia|
|H1 2026 shipments (low)|19,100|Smart Analytics Global|
|H1 2026 shipments (central)|more than 22,000|Counterpoint Research|
|H1 2026 shipments (high)|nearly 25,000|IDC|
|**GHSB floor / central / upper**|**34,718 / 37,618 / 40,618**|Axis Intelligence Research calculation|
**Formula:** GHSB = Omdia 2024 + Omdia 2025 + H1 2026 tracker estimate.
Floor uses Smart Analytics Global, central uses Counterpoint, upper uses IDC.
Pre-2024 units are excluded, so every reading is a floor on the true historical total.
This is the baseline reading.

A humanoid robot is a machine with two arms, two legs, hands and sensors, built to work in spaces designed for people.
The surprising part is that nobody agrees how many exist.
The International Federation of Robotics counted about 7,000 full-size humanoids sold in all of 2025.

IDC's higher figure includes robots that stand around 1.2 to 1.3 meters.
Later in 2026 IDC revised its 2025 baseline to about 18,500, and the first half of 2026 alone came in about 35 percent above that.

Humanoid robots crossed from demonstration into commercial deployment in 2026, and the shape of that transition is different from what the sector's pricing announcements implied.
Figure AI has a 40-unit fleet of Figure 03 robots working at BMW's largest assembly plant, billed at roughly $25 per robot-operating-hour.

content.text:
There isn’t one agreed count—it depends on what “commercial” means. If you mean **distinct humanoid models available to buy or lease**, recent industry trackers put the number at about **12–14**.[1][17]

If you mean **individual robots doing paid work**, there’s no reliable global total; deployments are still limited, and reported shipment numbers include many robots used for research, demonstrations, or pilots rather than commercial work.[6][11]
